My whole life I've farmed the same fields my father farmed. I'm 66 now, and my back isn't what it was, but I still know this land. Here in Quzhou, everybody grows winter wheat and summer maize — that's the rotation. I have about 10 mu. My son went to Handan city years ago, so I work it myself with my wife.

For wheat, I sow in October after the land cools. I use the 矮抗58 variety — I've grown it for years, it's stable, I know how it behaves. I plough the field before sowing, apply base fertilizer (diammonium phosphate and urea mixed), then topdress at jointing. I water four times: before winter freeze, returning green, jointing, and filling. Three spray passes — one for rust, one for aphids, one combined.

For maize, I plant right after I harvest the wheat in June — no time to waste. Hybrid seed, 郑单958, the co-op sells it and everyone uses it. I skip the plough and just rotary-till between the wheat stubble. I apply fertilizer at sowing and topdress at big bell stage. Summer rains usually cover most of the water needs but I irrigate twice if it's dry. Spray once or twice for corn borer and leaf blight.

I don't try new things much at my age. What I know works. The land gives me enough to live on.
